extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of French political history; readers interested in d'Argenson and 18th-century constitutional proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and interpret the principles and article-by-article provisions of the Plan for the Government of France (d'Argenson's constitution as published in the 1784 edition and contrasted with the 1737 draft). Focuses on decentralization to provincial and parish assemblies while preserving royal authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founding principles of the 1737 Considérations
rubrics_metrics.description: D'Argenson's 1737 work is founded upon two principles: (1) for rapid and decisive national action a strong and united government is necessary (Monarchy provides such government); and (2) the central government had taken upon itself multitudinous local concerns it could not supervise, producing neglect and disorder in local administration — thus local duties should be entrusted to popular control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the rationale for transferring parochial duties to locally elected committees while preserving overall royal authority; frames the Plan's objective to emancipate local administration from inefficient royal subalterns and invigorate provincial life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguard royal authority while devolving administration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plan repeatedly insists that in any introduction of local-reform the authority of the Crown must be scrupulously maintained (e.g., local bodies act under supervision and royal commissioners open and explain royal will).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D'Argenson designed devolved institutions (parish/district/provincial bodies) but kept instruments (Sub-delegates, Royal Commissioners, vetoes) to ensure the Crown's ultimate control — a deliberate 'divide et impera' balance to avoid undermining monarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article I: Provinces retained; feudal relations abolished; uniform internal administration; no tax exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The ancient divisions of the Realm into Provinces shall continue, though all feudal relation connected therewith shall hereby cease. The internal administration shall be uniform; no landed property shall be exempt from the common burdens and nobility or any office/dignity shall not exempt subjects from paying impositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to preserve provincial identity while removing feudal privileges and exemptions that distort taxation and administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article II: District divisions remain with mutual administrative independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The subsisting divisions of the Provinces into districts 'of greater or less extent' shall remain very much as before; they shall retain ancient usages, but shall be mutually independent in respect of administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeps existing territorial structure but grants administrative autonomy to districts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article III: Local subdivisions elect local officers from residents and property-holders
rubrics_metrics.description: Each District subdivided into cities, boroughs, and parishes shall have officers charged with finance and police chosen from persons living and holding property in the place; elections take place in an annual meeting (assemblée).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises local self-government via elected local officers responsible for routine civic duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article IV: Prepare Schedule of property and income for assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediate steps to prepare a Schedule or statement of property and income for each District to serve as the basis of assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes transparent fiscal bases for taxation and equitable assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article V: Annual District Assembly composition and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each District shall hold an annual Assembly lasting fifteen days, consisting of officers of the principal city, one deputy from each borough, and rotating officers from parishes; large landholders may attend. The Assembly transacts financial and other affairs and chooses deputies to represent the District in the Provincial Estates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets representative structure and meeting rhythm for district-level self-administration, with provision for broader participation by major landowners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article VI: Provincial Estates constituted by District deputies and certain great landholders
rubrics_metrics.description: In each Province there shall be Provincial Estates consisting of deputies chosen in District Assemblies and certain great landholders (Propriétaires) granted perpetual right to be present as the Peers of the Province.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an intermediate provincial deliberative body combining elected deputies with a limited, non-political presence of great landholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article VII: Nobility as ceremonial; no separate noble body in Estates
rubrics_metrics.description: Nobility who may attend the Estates shall have privileges of ceremony and none other; the nobility shall not constitute a separate body and no person of birth shall be present unless a deputy or a property-holder connecting him to the Province; Peers may be present by proxy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduces political privileges of nobility while allowing ceremonial status; prevents nobility forming a corporate political estate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article VIII: Executive officers for Estates and Districts (Syndic/Secretary/Treasurer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Provincial Estate shall have a Syndic-General, Secretary-General and Treasurer-General; each District Assembly shall have a Syndic, Secretary and Receiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies administrative offices and responsibilities; guidance includes extracts describing Treasurer-General duties and accountability between provincial treasuries and Royal Treasury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article IX: Royal Commissioners open Estates, explain contributions; Estates may present representations but cannot refuse imposed charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Provincial Estates are opened by four Royal Commissioners who explain the amount of contribution assessed; Estates are not optioned to refuse or modify charges imposed but may present representations which the Crown will receive and answer; Commissioners present regulations the Estates shall accept but may represent upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes procedure for Crown-to-province communication: the Crown sets contributions/regulations, explains reasons, and receives representations but retains decisive authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article X: Estates may propose provincial measures and dispose of matters not requiring royal sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: After arranging for execution of royal will, Estates may propose measures to the Crown and handle matters not requiring royal sanction finally by themselves, with Crown officers assisting them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants Estates limited initiative and autonomy on internal provincial affairs while preserving Crown prerogatives for matters requiring sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XI: Timing and executive commissions of Estates; deputies at Court
rubrics_metrics.description: Estates to meet end of November to early January; before dissolving they elect an executive commission (one deputy per District plus three principal officers) to hold until next Assembly; four deputies elected to reside at Court representing the Estates; District Assemblies likewise elect small executive commissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines temporal schedule and standing executive structures to ensure continuity between assemblies and representation at the royal court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XII: Royal Commissioners' subordinates limited powers and restraint on force
rubrics_metrics.description: Four Royal Commissioners may appoint subordinates to control troops and execute orders; these officers shall have no power to give orders in their own name or employ force against inhabitants except in last emergency and must report to superiors; salaries charged to general expenses; provincial executive maintenance charged to province.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits delegated royal force, centralises command with Commissioners, and financially separates royal salaries from provincial revenues to avoid abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XIII: Crown revenue collection by Provincial Estates; provincial revenue retained by Estates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Revenue of the Crown shall be collected by, and at the expense of, the Provincial Estates and paid entire into the Royal Treasury; Provincial Revenue shall be collected by, and remain at the absolute disposition of, the Estates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigns operational responsibility for tax collection to provincial bodies while preserving the flow of Crown revenues to Paris and provincial control over their own funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XIV: Accountability of Provincial Treasurers
rubrics_metrics.description: Provincial Treasurers shall be accountable to the Council of Finance and Chamber of Accounts at Paris for Crown revenues, and to the Provincial Estates for Provincial revenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates dual accountability to central financial organs for royal receipts and to provincial bodies for local finances, aiming for oversight and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XV: Suppression of many royal financial and administrative offices; transfer of duties to provinces; compensation for forfeiture
rubrics_metrics.description: Disappearance of Receivers-general, Receivers of Taille, Receivers-general of Domains and Woods, officers of Waters and Forests, Treasurers of Roads and Bridges, Treasurerships of France, Provincial Chambers of Accounts, Courts of Aides, and 'Élections' — their duties devolving to provincial and district administrations; persons subjected to forfeiture to receive compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A major administrative simplification and decentralisation, accompanied by compensation mechanisms to ease the transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XVI: Suppression of Governors and certain high military/judicial offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The offices of the Governors, Lieut.-Governors and Lieutenants of the Provinces, and also those of the 'Baillis d'épée,' shall be suppressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes old-personalised provincial executive posts to streamline provincial government under the Estates and Commissioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XVII: Resolution of disputes between local authorities by superior authority or Council
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions in dispute between different local authorities shall be decided, if possible, by the superior authority, or, in default, by the King's Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a mechanism for inter-local conflict resolution preserving hierarchical oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XVIII: Crown retains dispensation of justice; judicial administration unified; seigneurial jurisdictions suppressed
rubrics_metrics.description: The dispensation of justice shall remain the prerogative of the Crown; administration of justice shall be rendered uniform and high seigneurial jurisdictions shall be suppressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralises judicial authority while standardising procedure and abolishing feudal juridical privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XIX: Rules of judicial procedure (provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides certain rules of judicial procedure (details given in the Plan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates procedural reform to accompany judicial-uniformity goals; specific procedural provisions are part of the Plan's text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XX: Revision of laws, customs and charters only when contrary to equity/morality/public order
rubrics_metrics.description: The laws of the nation, local customs and corporate charters shall be revised but shall only be abrogated insofar as they may be found contrary to natural equity, morality, and public order. Preserve long-standing habits compatible with tranquillity and good police.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates cautious legal reform: preserve established, compatible local practices; remove only those inconsistent with equity and public order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XXI: Prescribed method of legal and customary revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescribes the method by which laws, customs and charters will be revised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes procedural safeguards and methods for systematic legal reform (specifics in Plan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XXII: Transitional administrative arrangements; suppression of venality of judicial charges with compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing administrative arrangements remain in force until promulgation of reforms; intention to suppress venality of judicial charges ('la vénalité des charges de judicature'); persons subjected to forfeiture will receive compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides transitional continuity and remedies for those economically affected by suppression of saleable offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XXIII: Pecuniary interest as guarantee for certain finance posts; suppression of survivances; measures for service efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: To certain posts in the department of Finance alone shall a pecuniary interest be attached as a guarantee for the integrity of the holders; the system of official reversions (survivances) shall be wholly suppressed; steps for efficiency of Crown administrative and judicial service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks to limit financial incentives to those necessary for integrity, abolish hereditary/survivance practices, and professionalise service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XXIV: Arrange payments of Royal officers in interest of the people; encourage prompt dispatch
rubrics_metrics.description: The payment of the Royal officers shall be arranged in the interests of the people to spare false expenses and so that superior and subordinate officers find as much benefit in prompt dispatch of affairs as in delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial reform intended to remove perverse incentives that encourage delay or unnecessary expense; succinct motto quoted: 'Il faut savoir économiser les graces les plus justes comme les supplices les plus sévères.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XXV: Clergy excluded from civil administration
rubrics_metrics.description: No person in holy orders shall henceforth be admitted to any share in the civil administration; constant civil work inconsistent with ecclesiastical duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separates ecclesiastical and civil roles to avoid conflicts of duty and ensure dedicated civil administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articles XXVI-XXVIII: Restrict appeals and reform Conseil des Parties
rubrics_metrics.description: No evocation of provincial causes for judgment in the capital (XXVI); appeals (requetes en cassation) shall be done away with so far as possible (XXVII); constitution of the 'Conseil des Parties' shall be reformed (XXVIII).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduces central judicial interference and reform appeals structures to strengthen local adjudication and judicial efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XXIX: Orders depriving liberty or removing persons require King's precise approval with ministerial report and signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Orders that deprive subjects of their liberty or remove them from domicile shall not be given without precise approval of the King's hand, which shall be granted only on the report of at least one minister, secretary or councillor of State guaranteeing justice and necessity and signing the presented sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adds a high-level safeguard to protect individual liberty from arbitrary orders by requiring explicit royal, ministerial guarantee and signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XXX: Abolish noble exemptions from taxation; reduce noble privileges to honorific rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Abolish distinctions that exempt nobles from taxes; reduce all noble privileges to purely honorific rights; make nobles share tax burdens with rest of subjects; preserve noble glory as honorific only and prevent it authorizing tyranny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major socio-fiscal egalitarian measure to equalise tax burden and reduce institutionalised noble privilege.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XXXI: Prohibition on purchase of noble patents
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall no longer be possible to buy a patent of nobility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closes commercial avenue to social status, preventing monetisation of noble rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XXXII: No proof of nobility required for official posts; nobles encouraged to serve
rubrics_metrics.description: In no charge, office, or post in connection with judicial or administrative bodies shall any proof of nobility be required; nobles are encouraged to serve and any temporary suspension of titles is not forever derogatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opens public service to non-nobles and allows nobles to participate without preserving privileged exclusive access; mitigates stigma of serving in lower offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XXXIII: Establishment of a heraldic Court
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides for the constitution of a heraldic Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an institutional body to oversee matters of heraldry and titles within the new framework (details in Plan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Article XXXIV: Maintain Catholic Establishment as public-moral base but limit political exclusion and avoid persecution; toleration where compatible with public order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Catholic Establishment shall be maintained as 'la base de la morale'; those unconvinced of its truths will be ineligible for public office, but no step shall be taken towards persecution or proscription; complete toleration is maintained insofar as compatible with public order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances religious establishment with limited civic exclusion (eligibility rule) while expressly forbidding persecution and allowing tolerated pluralism compatible with order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle that 'interest is more valuable than intelligence' for democratic development
rubrics_metrics.description: D'Argenson enunciates that in matters of government 'interest is more valuable than intelligence' — i.e., practical stake/interest in governance fosters political development among people lacking tradition or knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Plan rests on the republican-democratic belief that local engagement and vested interest will educate and civilize ordinary citizens into effective municipal magistrates.
